description: Reasoning vault for non-quadratic algebraic equations aligned with OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6: rational-exponent equations, higher-degree factoring and grouping, radical equations with extraneous-root checks, absolute value equations, quadratic-form substitution, and rational equations with domain exclusions.

archetypes.name: Solving Equations Involving Rational Exponents
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Solving Equations Involving Rational Exponents
archetypes.coreConcept: Isolate the base raised to a rational exponent u^(p/q) = k (in lowest terms), raise both sides to the reciprocal power q/p, and include ± when the numerator p is even.
archetypes.mentalModel: An even numerator p in u^(p/q) squares (or raises to an even power) the base first, erasing its sign—so undoing it must restore both + and - branches.
archetypes.governingRelation: u^{p/q} = k \implies u = \begin{cases} \pm k^{q/p} & \text{if } p \text{ is even and } k \ge 0 \\ k^{q/p} & \text{if } p \text{ is odd} \end{cases}

cognitiveTraps.description: Raising both sides of u^(p/q) = k to q/p when p is even and keeping only the positive branch +k^(q/p), omitting -k^(q/p).
Raising k to p/q instead of the reciprocal exponent q/p when solving u^(p/q) = k.

archetypes.figureNone: Rational-exponent equations solved algebraically; a graph would display the roots.

archetypes.name: Solving Higher-Degree Polynomial Equations by Factoring and Grouping
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Solving Equations Using Factoring
archetypes.coreConcept: Move all terms to one side so the right-hand side is 0, factor out the greatest common factor (including x^k), factor remaining polynomials by grouping or difference of squares, and apply the Zero Product Property.
archetypes.mentalModel: Factoring breaks a degree-3 or degree-4 equation into linear and quadratic factors; never divide by a variable expression that could equal 0.
archetypes.governingRelation: P(x) = 0 \implies x^k \cdot Q_1(x) \cdot Q_2(x) = 0 \implies x = 0 \lor Q_1(x) = 0 \lor Q_2(x) = 0

cognitiveTraps.description: Dividing both sides of an equation by x (or x^k) instead of factoring it out, silently discarding the root x = 0.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: x^3 = a x \implies x^2 = a \text{ (lost } x = 0\text{)}

cognitiveTraps.description: Solving a quadratic factor x^2 = a and reporting only x = +sqrt(a), omitting x = -sqrt(a).

archetypes.figureNone: Higher-degree polynomial equations solved by factoring; a graph would reveal the roots.

archetypes.name: Solving Radical Equations and Filtering Extraneous Roots
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Solving Radical Equations
archetypes.coreConcept: Isolate one radical on a side, square both sides to eliminate it (repeating if a second radical remains), solve the resulting algebraic equation, and substitute every candidate back into the original equation to reject extraneous roots.
archetypes.mentalModel: Squaring is not reversible: (-3)^2 = 3^2, so squaring can invent false roots where the isolated radical would have to equal a negative number.
archetypes.governingRelation: \sqrt{A(x)} = B(x) \implies A(x) = [B(x)]^2 \quad \text{with check } B(x) \ge 0 \text{ and } A(x) \ge 0

cognitiveTraps.description: Accepting every solution of the squared polynomial equation without checking whether it satisfies the original radical equation.
Squaring a binomial or unisolated sum term-by-term as (A + B)^2 = A^2 + B^2, omitting the middle term 2AB.

archetypes.figureNone: Radical equations solved algebraically; graphing both sides would show the intersection.

archetypes.name: Solving Absolute Value Equations
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Solving an Absolute Value Equation
archetypes.coreConcept: Isolate the absolute value expression |A(x)| = k; if k < 0 there is no solution, and if k >= 0 split into the two linear equations A(x) = k and A(x) = -k.
archetypes.mentalModel: Absolute value measures distance from zero: |A| = k asks which inputs place A at distance k on either the positive or negative side of 0.

cognitiveTraps.description: Dropping the absolute value bars and solving only the positive equation A(x) = k, omitting A(x) = -k.
Splitting |A(x)| = k into A(x) = k and A(x) = -k even when the isolated right-hand side k is negative.

archetypes.figureNone: Absolute value equations solved algebraically; a V-shaped graph would show the intersections.

archetypes.name: Solving Equations in Quadratic Form via u-Substitution
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Solving Other Types of Equations
archetypes.coreConcept: Recognize equations of the form a[f(x)]^2 + b[f(x)] + c = 0, substitute u = f(x) to solve the quadratic in u, and back-substitute each valid u-value into f(x) = u to find all solutions for x.
archetypes.mentalModel: Temporarily hiding the repeating expression f(x) inside u turns an unfamiliar higher-power or fractional-power equation into a standard quadratic.
archetypes.governingRelation: a[f(x)]^2 + b[f(x)] + c = 0 \xrightarrow{u = f(x)} au^2 + bu + c = 0 \implies f(x) = u_1 \lor f(x) = u_2

cognitiveTraps.description: Solving au^2 + bu + c = 0 for u and reporting the u-values directly without back-substituting f(x) = u to solve for x.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: x = u_1, u_2 \text{ instead of solving } f(x) = u_i

cognitiveTraps.description: When back-substituting u = x^2 over R, either omitting the ± roots for u > 0 or treating a negative u as giving real roots ±sqrt(|u|).

archetypes.figureNone: Quadratic-form equations solved algebraically by substitution; a graph would display the roots.

archetypes.name: Solving Rational Equations and Rejecting Domain-Excluded Roots
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §2.6 — Rational Equations & Domain Checks
archetypes.coreConcept: Identify all values of x that make any denominator zero, multiply every term on both sides by the least common denominator (LCD) to obtain a polynomial equation, solve it, and reject any candidate root that lies outside the domain.
archetypes.mentalModel: Multiplying by an expression containing x is only valid where that expression is nonzero; any candidate root that zeroes an original denominator was created by multiplying by 0.

cognitiveTraps.description: Reporting a candidate root obtained after clearing denominators even though it makes an original denominator equal to zero.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: D(x_0) = 0 \text{ ignored and } x_0 \text{ included in solution set}

cognitiveTraps.description: Multiplying only the fractional terms by the LCD while leaving non-fractional constant or integer terms unmultiplied.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: \frac{A}{D} + c = \frac{B}{D} \implies A + c = B \text{ instead of } A + cD = B

archetypes.figureNone: Rational equations solved algebraically; a graph would show roots and vertical asymptotes.
